from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Prerequisite: The Polarization Filter", ["Light waves oscillate in all directions.", "Polarizers act like vertical fences.", "Only vertical oscillations pass through."])
        
        # Assets
        light_wave = VGroup(
            *[Line(ORIGIN, UP*0.5, color=WHITE).shift(RIGHT*i*0.2) for i in range(-5, 6)],
            *[Line(ORIGIN, RIGHT*0.5, color=WHITE).shift(UP*i*0.2) for i in range(-5, 6)]
        )
        fence = Rectangle(height=3, width=0.1, color="#8888FF", fill_opacity=0.5)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.place_at_grid(light_wave, 'C2', scale_factor=0.5)
        self.play(Create(light_wave), run_time=2)
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.place_at_grid(fence, 'C4', scale_factor=1.0)
        self.play(FadeIn(fence), run_time=1)
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#8888FF")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        polarized_wave = VGroup(*[Line(ORIGIN, UP*0.5, color=WHITE).shift(RIGHT*i*0.2) for i in range(5, 10)])
        self.place_at_grid(polarized_wave, 'C5', scale_factor=0.5)
        label = Text("Polarized Light", font_size=20, color="#FFFF00")
        self.place_at_grid(label, 'D5', scale_factor=0.8)
        
        self.play(
            FadeOut(light_wave),
            FadeIn(polarized_wave),
            Write(label),
            run_time=2
        )
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#FFFF00")
        self.wait(2)

class Section2Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Introduction to Optical Activity", ["Sugar molecules are chiral.", "They physically twist light.", "This is optical activity."])
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Mathematical Visualization: The Rotating Vector", [
            "Vector rotation represents light.", 
            "Angle θ depends on distance.", 
            "Different wavelengths rotate differently."
        ])
        
        # Define objects
        vector = Arrow(ORIGIN, UP * 1.5, color="#00FFFF")
        formula = MathTex(r"\theta = [\alpha] \cdot c \cdot L", font_size=36)
        
        # Position initial objects
        self.place_at_grid(vector, 'C3')
        self.place_at_grid(formula, 'B4')
        
        # Red and Blue wavelength indicators
        red_vec = Arrow(ORIGIN, UP * 1.2, color=RED)
        blue_vec = Arrow(ORIGIN, UP * 1.2, color=BLUE)
        self.place_at_grid(red_vec, 'E3')
        self.place_at_grid(blue_vec, 'E5')

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#00FFFF")
        self.play(GrowArrow(vector))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#FFFFFF")
        self.play(Write(formula))
        self.play(Rotate(vector, angle=PI/2, about_point=vector.get_start()))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#FFFF00")
        self.play(
            GrowArrow(red_vec),
            GrowArrow(blue_vec)
        )
        self.play(
            Rotate(red_vec, angle=2*PI, rate_func=linear, run_time=3),
            Rotate(blue_vec, angle=4*PI, rate_func=linear, run_time=3)
        )
        self.wait(1)

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lines = ["White light contains many colors.", "Each color rotates differently.", "The analyzer reveals color bands.", "Rotating it creates movement.", "The barber pole effect appears."]
        self.setup_layout("The Barber Pole Effect", lines)
        
        # Mobjects for animations
        beaker = Cylinder(radius=0.5, height=2, color=BLUE_D, fill_opacity=0.3)
        self.place_at_grid(beaker, 'D3')
        
        # Bands
        bands = VGroup(*[Line(UP*0.5, DOWN*0.5, color=c) for c in [RED, GREEN, BLUE]])
        bands.arrange(RIGHT, buff=0.1)
        self.place_at_grid(bands, 'D3')
        
        # Analyzer
        analyzer = Square(side_length=1.5, color=YELLOW).rotate(PI/4)
        self.place_at_grid(analyzer, 'D5')
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(YELLOW))
        self.play(Create(beaker))
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(GREEN))
        self.play(FadeIn(bands))
        self.play(Rotate(bands, angle=PI/4, run_time=2))
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(BLUE))
        self.play(Create(analyzer))
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[3].animate.set_color(RED))
        self.play(Rotate(analyzer, angle=PI/2, run_time=2))
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[4].animate.set_color(GOLD))
        self.play(Indicate(bands))
        self.wait(1)

class Section5Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Practical Application: The Sugar Concentration Sensor", 
                          ["Rotation indicates sugar concentration.", 
                           "We measure this angle precisely.", 
                           "This enables non-invasive testing."])
        
        # 1. Show a light source, beaker, and detector setup.
        laser = Line(start=LEFT, end=RIGHT, color=RED).set_length(1)
        beaker = Square(side_length=1.5, color=BLUE).set_fill(BLUE, opacity=0.3)
        detector = Rectangle(height=1.5, width=0.5, color=WHITE).set_fill(GREY, opacity=0.8)
        
        # Positions
        self.place_at_grid(laser, 'C1')
        self.place_at_grid(beaker, 'C3')
        self.place_at_grid(detector, 'C5')
        
        self.play(Create(laser), Create(beaker), Create(detector))
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture_mobjects[0].animate.set_color("#FFD700"))
        
        # 2. Label the detector output with 'Concentration %' in #00FF00.
        concentration_label = Text("Conc: 0%", font_size=24, color="#00FF00")
        self.place_at_grid(concentration_label, 'D5')
        self.play(Write(concentration_label))
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture_mobjects[1].animate.set_color("#FFD700"))
        
        # 3. Visualize the concentration change adjusting the detected angle.
        # Rotating laser polarization as light passes through
        beam = Line(start=laser.get_right(), end=detector.get_left(), color=YELLOW)
        self.add(beam)
        
        angle_tracker = ValueTracker(0)
        beam.add_updater(lambda m: m.rotate(angle_tracker.get_value(), about_point=laser.get_right()))
        
        self.play(angle_tracker.animate.set_value(PI/6), run_time=2)
        concentration_label.add_updater(lambda m: m.become(Text(f"Conc: {int(angle_tracker.get_value()*20)}%", font_size=24, color="#00FF00").move_to(self.grid['D5'])))
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture_mobjects[2].animate.set_color("#FFD700"))
        self.wait(2)

outline.topic: The Barber Pole Effect: Polarization and Chirality in Sugar Water

sections.title: Prerequisite: The Polarization Filter
sections.content: Explain that light is an electromagnetic wave oscillating in all directions. A polarizer acts like a vertical fence, allowing only waves oscillating in one specific plane to pass through.
sections.example: Visualize a vibrating string passing through a vertical slit in a board; only the vertical oscillations remain.

sections.title: Introduction to Optical Activity
sections.content: Introduce chiral molecules (like sugar/sucrose). These molecules have a 'handedness' that physically twists the electric field vector of polarized light as it travels through a solution.
sections.example: Imagine a corkscrew moving through honey; the shape of the screw forces it to rotate as it advances.

sections.title: Mathematical Visualization: The Rotating Vector
sections.content: Represent the light vector as an arrow on a 2D plane. As the light travels through length 'L', the angle of rotation 'θ' is given by θ = [α] * c * L, where [α] is the specific rotation. Use a rotating clock-hand animation to show how different wavelengths rotate at different speeds.
sections.example: A clock hand shifting its 12:00 position to 3:00 as the light enters the beaker, showing the phase shift graphically.

sections.title: The Barber Pole Effect (The Core Phenomenon)
sections.content: When white light (composed of all colors) passes through a sugar solution and then a second polarizer (analyzer), each color is rotated by a different amount. Rotating the analyzer creates a 'barber pole' visual effect, where rainbow colors appear to climb or descend the beaker.
sections.example: A 3D animation of a glass cylinder where bands of red, green, and blue light rotate at different pitch angles, resembling a rotating barber pole.

sections.title: Practical Application: The Sugar Concentration Sensor
sections.content: Connect the phenomenon to real-world utility: Saccharimetry. By measuring the angle of rotation, we can determine the exact concentration of sugar in a solution.
sections.example: An automated 'Sugar-Bot' character uses a laser and a sensor to check the sweetness of a fruit juice sample in a factory line without touching it.
